subject: POC trial environment planning — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC: trial environment options & proposed success criteria

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — great to hear more about the Acme.ai use case and the compliance requirements around customer data. Per our conversation, I wanted to recap proposed success criteria and outline environment options so we can pick the right trial approach.

Proposed high-level success criteria (attached as a doc):
- Latency: 95th perc <= 350ms for 1k concurrent inference QPS
- Cost: < $0.015 per 1k tokens for average payloads using batching & caching
- Functional: consistent generation quality vs baseline prompts (we'll run 3 eval suites)
- Security: data stays within Acme VPC; logs retained per your retention policy

Environment options we discussed:
1) Hosted Redwood sandbox (fastest to start, easiest for iteration)
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool; predictable throughput but slightly longer setup)
3) VPC trial / Private deployment (customer-managed VPC connectivity; best for compliance)

Questions / ask:
- Which env do you prefer for the POC? Given compliance notes, VPC is likely preferred but we can propose a hybrid where we start hosted for early evals and move to VPC for full e2e tests.
- Confirm POA: who on your side owns procurement/network (Priya?) and who will be the technical owner for onboarding?
- Target timeline: do you want a ~3–4 week POC or a shorter 2-week pilot?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm env choice and owners by EOD Friday
- We share a draft VPC onboarding checklist + network requirements (attached)
- Schedule a kickoff with infra + security (send 30-min slot options)

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.docx, VPC_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: trial environment options & proposed success criteria

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. Priya and I reviewed with our security team this morning. Confirming:
- We prefer a VPC trial so that all inference traffic and logs remain in our VPC. This is a hard requirement for the POC (data residency + audit).
- Technical owners: Priya Shah (procurement/network) and Alex Johnson (platform lead) will be primary contacts.

Success criteria feedback:
- Latency: the 95th <= 350ms target looks good; we may relax to 400ms for cold-start windows during early testing.
- Eval suites: we'll provide the 3 prompt sets and a small labeled baseline for quality comparison.
- Cost: we'll treat cost numbers as directional during the POC; main focus is performance & security.

Timeline: we are aiming for a 4-week POC that ends mid-September. First week: onboarding & infra; weeks 2–3: functional tests and load; week 4: tuning and final metrics.

Network question: what inbound/outbound firewall rules and IP ranges will Redwood need to peer with our VPC? Also, do you support private connectivity via AWS Transit Gateway / VPC peering?

If you can share the VPC onboarding checklist + a proposed kickoff window next week, we can lock in a date.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Platform Lead, Acme.ai
alex.johnson@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: trial environment options & proposed success criteria

Alex / Priya —

Great — VPC trial it is. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

Network/connectivity: We support VPC peering, Transit Gateway, and PrivateLink. For the POC we recommend either Transit Gateway or VPC peering depending on your architecture; I'll have Rishi share specific CIDR and ports. High level requirements:
- Outbound: Redwood egress IP ranges for control-plane callbacks (we'll provide the list)
- Inbound: we use mutual TLS for control-plane and short-lived certs for runtime nodes; you will need to allow connections on ports 443 and 10000–10010 for telemetry/KV cache (details in checklist).

Proposed POC plan & timeline (aligned to your 4-week ask):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize owners & sign off on networking doc; sign PO (if needed)
- Week 1: Redwood infra provisions VPC trial, we run basic smoke tests (Rishi lead)
- Weeks 2–3: Functional & load tests, quality evals (Monica + SEs lead)
- Week 4: Tuning, cost analysis, final metrics & demo to stakeholders

Owners:
- Infra / connectivity: Rishi Malhotra (redwood) — rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
- Onboarding & SE coordination: Monica Patel (redwood) — monica.patel@redwood.com
- Platform lead & procurement (customer): Alex Johnson / Priya Shah

Next steps action items:
1) Alex/Priya: confirm kickoff slots for next Tue/Thu morning (we sent 3 options in Calendly link)
2) Redwood: Rishi to share IP ranges + exact firewall rules by 08/07
3) Acme: provide the 3 prompt sets and labeled baseline by 08/10

Attachments: VPC_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (detailed network requirements), redwood-poc-pricing.xlsx (pricing for dedicated/reserved options)

If that all looks good I'll schedule the kickoff and loop in our security engineer.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks — please ack and I'll set a 30-min internal sync if needed.
